focus: Define the default-on integration reference design (reviewer grader slot): requirements, measured cost, risk ledger, and the final ranked recommendations.
noveltyJustification: Workflow-route citations, the fixture inertness observation, the D4 method-naming dependency, the batched run proposal, and the final ranked recommendation table are new.
keyQuestions: What drove the measured Jev result?
How can accuracy improve or cost fall?
How can the measurement become more trustworthy?
Where else in .skilled would the same judgment pay off?
What would default-on integration need, cost, and risk?
answeredQuestions: What would default-on integration need, cost, and risk?
ruledOut: Flipping the grader default on today's corpus: the fallback is inert there and the only miss population is synthetic.
Treating the version pin as drift protection by itself: it needs a stored report to compare against.
Treating the payload question as settled by --accept-payload: a live policy needs an explicit decision.
focusTrackReason: The integration question closes the loop from measurement to enablement using the reviewer grader slot as the reference design.

title: Default-on has one concrete home and it is inert today
claim: The reviewer workflow routes scoring_method=reviewer to reviewer-scorer with --grader noop|mock|llm behind SPECKIT_REVIEWER_BENCHMARKS; the shipped profile has 8 fixture hits and 0 misses, so a Jev grader would never fire until miss fixtures exist.

title: The minimum integration surface is small and enumerable
claim: A jev grader value reusing the frozen question and options, a verdictMethod naming decision for D4, availability and skip behavior, a payload policy, usage/model/latency telemetry with requalify, and an opt-in enablement order are the complete change set.

title: Reference-design cost is small at benchmark volume and the one-call variant is recomputable
claim: 73 calls for 24 rows at p50 334 ms and 16,767 estimated tokens; one-call would be 24 calls with identical picks on this corpus; a batched run request carrying the three orders is an untested one-request option; reviewer-regression has only 8 merged cases.

title: The risk ledger is ordered by corpus validity first
claim: Corpus validity, payload egress, false confidence at 24 rows, version drift and availability, forced choice without abstention, and cost creep are the risks; the corpus risk invalidates a default-on decision before any technical one.

title: The measurement-to-integration loop is designed end to end and unexercised
claim: Reviewer runs write reviewer-report.json with per_test verdictMethod; the fallback census reads pattern/llm-grader/none per report; misses would be labeled and judged by the same keep rule; none of it has run because no report exists and live outputs are hashed.

title: Final ranked recommendations issued
claim: Seven ranked items: natural corpus and labels (required), trust package (required), one-call protocol and usage/cache (recommended), opt-in jev grader with miss fixtures (recommended), shared harness reuse (recommended), widening/batch pricing (optional), and no model read in completion detection.
